_: The role vocabulary a screen spec is written in.
A spec that names Button and Field can only be built on a library that has a
Button and a Field. A spec that names `primaryAction` and `textInput` can be
built on any library that binds those roles — which is what makes one agreed
screen reachable on more than one stack.
The vocabulary is deliberately small. Every role here is one a product screen
actually asks for; anything a specific library adds beyond this is reached by
naming its component directly, and that spec stops being portable. That is a
fair trade to make knowingly, not by accident.
Axes are the props a spec may set. They carry the same meaning on every
library; each binding says what the library calls them and which of its values

roles.pageHeader: Names the screen and holds its primary action.
roles.heading: A title inside the screen.
roles.primaryAction: The one action the screen exists for.
roles.secondaryAction: A supporting action, subordinate to the primary one.
roles.iconAction: An action shown as an icon only; it always needs an accessible name.
roles.textInput: Single-line text entry with a label.
roles.searchInput: Text entry that filters what is on screen.
roles.select: Choice from a short fixed list.
roles.checkbox: Independent on/off choice, applied on submit.
roles.list: Vertical run of items with no columns to compare.
roles.statusTag: Compact label carrying a status or category.
roles.avatar: Visual stand-in for a person or entity.
roles.divider: The one hairline rule between content.
roles.inlineMessage: Message that stays until the condition is resolved.
roles.transientMessage: Message that leaves on its own.
roles.loading: Busy indicator for an unmeasurable wait.
roles.skeleton: Placeholder holding the shape of content that has not arrived.
roles.emptyState: What the screen shows when there is nothing to show.
roles.pagination: Page navigation for a known total.
roles.tooltip: Short text on hover or focus.
roles.dialog: Modal window for a task that interrupts the screen.

size.means: the element's place on the density scale
